title: The Erdős–Straus count is governed by a quadratic L-value
description:
An experimental route from solution-counting to L(1,χp), with a machine-verified account of the wall.

Let f(p) denote the number of unordered positive solutions of 4/p = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z. Building on the divisor-sum framework of Elsholtz and Tao (2013), we report an empirical law verified across 278,570 primes of the six hard residue classes mod 840 from 73 to 2.01×109: f(p) ≈ (log p)3 · L(1,χp)−c, with corr(ln f, ln L(1,χp)) = −0.62. The more primes split in Q(√p), the fewer Erdős–Straus solutions p has.

The Erdős–Straus conjecture is open; nothing here proves or disproves it. The contribution is a measured, reproducible, structurally-identified law for the solution count, a machine-verified delimitation (Lean 4 + Mathlib, 20 theorems) of why the elementary toolbox cannot close the problem, and a map of the analytic wall the law runs into.

This record contains the paper together with its computational artifacts: solution-count datasets, analysis code, computation engines, and the Lean 4 development.
